title: Elevator races and failover
idea: Concurrency bugs in an elevator system come from many panels and sensors acting at once; the fix makes each check-and-claim atomic and treats a silent car as failed.

analogy.text: Two receptionists hear the same phone call and both send a porter. A shared logbook that only one person writes at a time sends one porter.
analogy.breaks: A logbook is slow; the map's atomic step is not.

points: Two panels both see no open call, then both dispatch a car.
On a `ConcurrentHashMap`, `computeIfAbsent` checks and inserts as one atomic step.
A car silent for longer than the timeout is declared stuck.
Its open hall calls move to a healthy car; an alarm calls an operator.

hero.title: Two panels, one UP call on floor 5

steps.caption: Unsafe version. Panel A checks whether 5:UP is already open.
Before A writes, panel B checks too. The map is still empty.
Both threads now hold the answer no. Neither knows about the other.
A dispatches E1 and writes it to the map.
B acts on its stale no, overwrites the entry, and dispatches E2 too. Two cars for one call.
Safe version. Both threads call `computeIfAbsent` at the same moment.
The map runs the function once for this key. One car is dispatched.
The other call gets the existing value back and dispatches nothing.

code.title: Prove the race
code.caption: A barrier forces both threads to look before either writes, so the race shows up every run.

walk.text: Run the same race twice: check-then-act first, then atomic.
A thread-safe map, a two-thread barrier, and a dispatch counter.
Safe: `computeIfAbsent` runs the function for only one caller per key.
Unsafe: both look, wait for each other, then both put and dispatch.
Join both threads before reading the count, so the output is stable.

code.title: Stuck car failover
code.caption: Times are passed in, so the failure replays the same way every run.

walk.text: Two cars report in at t=0, and three hall calls are assigned.
E1 keeps reporting; E2 goes silent. Sweeps run at 20 and 40 seconds.
A heartbeat from a car already marked down is ignored until inspected.
New calls skip a down car and go to the first healthy one.
A sweep marks silent cars down and moves their calls to a healthy car.
With no healthy car left it throws, so the caller must raise an outage alarm.

pitfalls: Never pair `containsKey` with `put`; use `computeIfAbsent` on a `ConcurrentHashMap`.
Guard each car's stop set with one lock, or feed it through one queue.
Do not trust a recovered car automatically; require an operator check first.

quiz.q: What does CarFailover print right after the t=40 alarm?
quiz.why: E2 was silent for 40 seconds, past the 30-second timeout. The sweep marks it down and `replaceAll` moves both its calls to E1.

takeaway: Make check-and-claim atomic, and fail over silent cars to healthy ones.

starters: Why is a ConcurrentHashMap alone not enough here?
Should each Elevator run on its own thread with a command queue?
What should happen to riders inside a stuck car?
